criteria.criterion: Crash repair: a test has a main first-parent commit whose tree and parent match a landing-intent and that has no landing record. Reconcile writes the landing record from the intent alone, with the host making no call. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: crash_between_merge_and_landing_is_repaired_from_the_intent_alone passed. It asserts host.calls()==0 against a host that would return an error, one Repaired finding with Source::Intent and PR 7, one landing with host_commit equal to the merged commit and the intent id that validates, and that a second run writes nothing new.

criteria.criterion: Host unavailable: a commit with no matching intent and an erroring host gives an 'unattributed' finding and writes no landing record. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: unavailable_host_gives_unattributed_and_writes_nothing passed. It asserts one Unattributed finding whose reason contains 'host unavailable', that the line says 'unattributed', no landings, and an unchanged records tip.

criteria.criterion: No guessing: a commit with no intent and no merged PR is reported unattributed and nothing is written. It is never attributed to a nearby intent or PR. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: no_intent_and_no_pull_request_is_reported_never_guessed passed. It has nearby intents 1 and 2 and three host answers: none, an unknown PR #99, and PR 1 with the wrong head. Each run gives Unattributed, no landing, and an unchanged records tip. The code also reports several matching intents as unattributed rather than picking one (reconcile.rs:309), and parse_merged_pr returns an error for several merged PRs.

criteria.criterion: Host fallback: with no matching intent and the host naming the merged PR, the landing record is written for that PR. Commits that already have a landing record are skipped. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: host_names_the_merged_pull_request_when_no_intent_matches passed. Intent 7's base no longer matches; the host names PR 7 with the same head. The test asserts a Repaired finding with Source::Host and that the landing names intent 7. The host is called once, only for the merged commit. The already-landed commit and the declared-intervention commit are skipped, and the first landing is untouched.

criteria.criterion: Bound: commits before the first landing-intent record on athena/records, and before the last landing record, are never reconciled. When the records branch is absent or holds no intent, reconcile does nothing and reports that. A test covers both cases. Check with `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: bound_skips_older_commits_and_absent_or_empty_records passed. Case A: only the commit after the last landing is examined, and the host is never asked about older commits; the known-gap crashed commit is deliberately not reconciled. Case B (no records branch) skips with 'does not exist'. Case C (branch with no intent) skips with 'no landing intent'. B and C have no findings, no host calls and no writes.

criteria.criterion: `athena land` and `athena status` run reconcile first, and an unattributed commit appears in their output. A test shows this. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria.evidence: I ran the CLI integration tests status_reports_an_unattributed_main_commit_and_writes_nothing and land_reports_an_unattributed_main_commit_before_it_does_anything_else; both passed. They run the real athena binary with a fake failing gh on PATH. The output contains 'unattributed' and the stray sha, `--json` shows outcome 'unattributed', and no landing is written. main.rs now calls status_with_reconcile. Athena::land_pr calls reconcile before resolving the job, and it is the only land path (`pr: _` in main.rs). Athena's recorded runs: fmt, clippy and the full test suite (1081 tests) passed.

findings.summary: Scope drift: the new file crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs is not on the expected deliverables list, and the listed land.rs is unchanged.
findings.evidence: The test file was added to show criterion 6, so it adds no behaviour scope. The land wiring went into gh.rs `Athena::land_pr`, which is the only path behind `athena land`. Neither drift leaves a criterion unshown.

findings.summary: The host fallback writes a landing only when an unfulfilled intent records the PR number and head the host named. A PR merged without any intent stays unattributed.
findings.evidence: This is a reasonable reading, because a landing record names its intent. It matches §8.1 step 4 and is stated in the CHANGELOG and module docs. It is still narrower than a literal reading of 'asks the host which pull request merged … and writes the missing landing record'.

findings.summary: In gh.rs, the new test sits above the existing `use` lines in the test module.
findings.evidence: `parse_merged_pr_keeps_only_the_pull_request_that_merged_the_commit` comes before `use serde_json::json;` and the other imports.

summary: Verdict: pass. All eight acceptance criteria are met and nothing blocks the change. I ran the six reconcile unit tests in athena-core and the two new CLI integration tests; all eight passed. They cover four cases: a landing record missing after a crash is repaired from its intent alone, with no host call; an unavailable host gives 'unattributed' and nothing is written; a commit is never guessed onto a nearby intent or pull request; and when the host names the merged pull request, the record is written and already-named commits are skipped. They also check the walk's bound and the two empty-records cases. Reconcile now runs first in both `athena status` (text and `--json`) and `athena land`. The integration tests run the real binary with a fake `gh` that fails every call, and the unattributed commit shows in the output. For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I relied on Athena's recorded passing runs rather than rerunning them. The change matches docs/design/records-history.md §8.1, the CHANGELOG entry cites §8.1, D111 and job 3 part 2, and no dependency or governance file was changed. I found three small issues. First, a new test file is not on the deliverables list, and the land wiring went into gh.rs instead of the listed land.rs. Second, the host fallback writes a record only when a landing intent records the pull request the host names, so a pull request merged with no intent stays unattributed. This is documented and consistent with §8.1. Third, a test in gh.rs is placed above that module's imports.
